nodes.summary: For real nodes $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ and indices $k \ne j$ below $n$, the $k$-th evaluated Lagrange basis polynomial $\ell_k$ for these nodes satisfies $\ell_k(x_j) = 0$.
nodes.title: Lagrange basis polynomials vanish at the other nodes

nodes.summary: If the real nodes $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ are pairwise distinct, then $\ell_k(x_k) = 1$ for every $k < n$, where $\ell_k$ is the $k$-th evaluated Lagrange basis polynomial for these nodes.
nodes.title: Lagrange basis polynomials equal one at their own node

nodes.summary: For real nodes $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, an index $k < n$ and a real number $t$, the value at $t$ of the $k$-th Lagrange basis polynomial is $\ell_k(t) = \prod_{j \ne k} (x_k - x_j)^{-1} (t - x_j)$, the product running over the indices $j < n$ with $j \ne k$.
nodes.title: Evaluated Lagrange basis polynomial

nodes.summary: If the real nodes $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ are pairwise distinct, then for every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and every $j < n$, the Lagrange interpolant of $f$ on these nodes satisfies $\mathcal{L}^n f(x_j) = f(x_j)$.
nodes.title: The Lagrange interpolant matches the function at the nodes

nodes.summary: For real nodes $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a real number $t$, the Lagrange interpolant of $f$ at $t$ is $\mathcal{L}^n f(t) = \sum_{k < n} f(x_k)\, \ell_k(t)$, where $\ell_k$ is the $k$-th evaluated Lagrange basis polynomial for these nodes.
nodes.title: Lagrange interpolant

nodes.summary: If the real nodes $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ are pairwise distinct, then their Lebesgue function satisfies $L_n(x_j) = 1$ for every $j < n$.
nodes.title: The Lebesgue function equals one at the nodes

nodes.summary: For real nodes $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ and a real number $t$, the Lebesgue function of the nodes at $t$ is $L_n(t) = \sum_{k < n} |\ell_k(t)|$, where $\ell_k$ is the $k$-th evaluated Lagrange basis polynomial for these nodes.
nodes.title: Lebesgue function

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
